banned.fingerprint: A two-line headline on the left, the lede and two buttons in a right column, and a framed app window straddling a full-bleed colour band below.
banned.why: Every SaaS page since 2019. A new palette does not make it new.

banned.fingerprint: A centered headline and buttons over a centered screenshot, followed by three equal icon cards.
banned.why: The template that templates are made from.

banned.fingerprint: A big headline with lede and buttons on the left and a product card, device render, or document on the right.
banned.why: The second most common hero after the split-straddle; the object is a prop, not the world.

banned.fingerprint: The last line or word of the headline switched to the accent colour.
banned.why: A colour swap is the cheapest emphasis there is; take emphasis from the world instead.

banned.fingerprint: Numbered how-it-works rows, rounded pricing cards with one dark recommended plan, a plain chevron FAQ list, and a two-column footer in sequence.
banned.why: The kit makes every product page a sibling of every other.

banned.fingerprint: A giant full-width headline, then the lede on the left with buttons on the right, then the demo panel below.
banned.why: The template that replaced the split-straddle once colours and worlds changed.

banned.fingerprint: Torn edges, perforations, barcodes, sprocket holes, or screw heads on a page whose world is not that artifact.
banned.why: The default 'material' costume; it blurs the one world the page commits to.

banned.fingerprint: A headline broken in two with a product band, card, or strip laid between its lines.
banned.why: Round 7 judges blamed it for every hierarchy point lost; the variety review saw it repeated across pages.

banned.fingerprint: A giant headline at top left on a pale grey or off-white page over a framed app panel (border, shadow, title bar), whatever the world.
banned.why: Round 7 variety review: the shared Wingman skeleton.

compositions.name: Product as stage
compositions.move: The working product scene fills the first viewport edge to edge; the headline is set inside the scene's own frame, like a window title, a plate, or a caption on the stage.
compositions.rhythm: Later sections zoom into one region of the same scene at a larger scale, so the page reads as one continuous product.
compositions.mobile: The scene shows one pane; the headline sits above it, and the pane tabs live inside the frame.
compositions.risk: Fails if the scene is a static screenshot or a dashboard collage.

compositions.name: Typographic wall
compositions.move: Display type at 11-16vw owns the first viewport as one unbroken block, set on or cut into the artifact; the live product moment sits directly beneath it or behind it, never between its lines.
compositions.rhythm: Each section opens with one oversized word that carries meaning, then the artifact.
compositions.mobile: Type sets at 18-22vw on two to four lines; the product moment follows the headline as one full-width strip.
compositions.risk: Fails when the line breaks fall where the words do, not where the meaning does.

compositions.name: Specimen index
compositions.move: The page is a catalogue: a large title, then an index of the product's real parts (sensors, rules, capabilities), each row a specimen with its own small live scene at a different scale.
compositions.rhythm: Rows alternate scale and density; one row expands into a full-bleed spread.
compositions.mobile: Each specimen becomes a full-width card with its scene on top and a one-line label.
compositions.risk: Fails if the rows become equal cards; vary scale or it is a feature grid.

compositions.name: Headline on the artifact
compositions.move: One artifact of the world fills the first viewport at a scale that crops off at least one edge; the headline and actions are set on its surface: printed on the face, stamped on the sheet, posted on the board.
compositions.rhythm: The artifact returns in later sections, cut away, annotated, or continued (the next page of the register, the rest of the roll).
compositions.mobile: The artifact fills the width and keeps the headline on its surface; secondary detail moves below it.
compositions.risk: Fails as clip art or as a render beside the headline; it must carry the headline and the product's output.

compositions.name: Scroll sequence
compositions.move: A sticky stage holds one product scene while the copy scrolls past it in steps; each step changes the scene (a day passes, a request is traced, an invoice is issued and paid).
compositions.rhythm: The sequence is the how-it-works section; everything before it is short and everything after it is quiet.
compositions.mobile: A stepper with the stage above and Previous / Next controls; never a long scroll past an empty pinned panel.
compositions.risk: Fails with empty stretches; every step must change the stage, and the step list stays dense.

compositions.name: The page is an instrument
compositions.move: One large visitor-operated control (dial, slider, timeline scrubber, toggle) drives a full-width visualization of the product's result; the headline names what the control changes.
compositions.rhythm: Later sections re-use the same control language at smaller scale (pricing seats, plan toggle).
compositions.mobile: The control spans the full width at a 44px or larger hit area, directly under the visualization it drives.
compositions.risk: Fails if the control changes nothing meaningful or needs instructions.

compositions.name: Artifact thread
compositions.move: The story is told by real-looking artifacts in one column: messages, receipts, logs, tickets, at their native sizes and materials, each one annotated with a single line.
compositions.rhythm: The column widens at two moments into full-bleed spreads where artifacts collect into the product's outcome.
compositions.mobile: Native: the column is already phone-shaped; annotations move from the margin to above each artifact.
compositions.risk: Fails if artifacts are generic cards; each needs its own material and anatomy.

compositions.name: Broadsheet grid
compositions.move: A strict 12-column editorial grid with a masthead, a lead story (the thesis with the product scene as its photograph), and secondary columns at different widths.
compositions.rhythm: Column structure changes per section (8/4, 3/9, 6/6) while the baseline grid stays fixed.
compositions.mobile: One column with the masthead compressed; secondary stories become collapsible sections.
compositions.risk: Avoid italic serif with mono kicker labels; that is the AI editorial cluster.

color.name: Drenched
color.rule: The page is one saturated hue at 60% or more of its area; text is near-black or white at full contrast; one neutral surface holds the product scene.

color.name: Deep coloured stage
color.rule: A dark field in a chromatic hue (ink blue, oxblood, forest, aubergine), never near-black with neon; the product scene is the brightest thing on the page.

color.name: Paper, ink, one spot
color.rule: The world's own paper (manila, newsprint, ledger buff, kraft) at a visible tint, true ink, and one spot colour used on 5% of the page or less, always on the thing that matters (the action, the alert, the total). Never a neutral near-white.

color.name: Semantic palette as brand
color.rule: The product's own status scale (air quality bands, VAT rules, severity, sentiment) becomes the brand palette; every colour on the page means something.

color.name: Duotone
color.rule: Two inks only, plus paper; every graphic, chart, and illustration is drawn in those two, including the product scene's accents.

color.name: Tonal monochrome
color.rule: One hue in six or more tints and shades carries every surface; contrast comes from value, not from a second colour.

color.name: Committed bands
color.rule: Full-bleed bands of one saturated hue alternate with paper; the bands carry the product moments. Not under a straddling app window.

devices.name: Measurement rulers
devices.rule: Tick marks, scales, and axis labels with real units frame sections and the product scene.

devices.name: Numerals as ornament
devices.rule: One true number per section, set large inside the artifact with tabular figures in the text face (412 ms, 9 EUR, 800 ppm), and always smaller than that section's heading.

devices.name: Cutaway diagram
devices.rule: An SVG cutaway or exploded view of the object with leader lines and labels explains how it works.

devices.name: Paper artifacts
devices.rule: Receipt edges, perforations, stamps, and folds give documents a material; one artifact per section at most.

devices.name: Margin annotations
devices.rule: Short handwritten-weight notes with leader lines point at exact parts of the product scene instead of separate feature copy.

devices.name: Signal traces
devices.rule: Waveforms, sparklines, or level meters drawn from the Sample data run through the page as connective tissue.

devices.name: Visible grid
devices.rule: The layout grid is drawn as hairlines and becomes structure; content snaps to it and occasionally breaks it on purpose.

devices.name: Index tabs
devices.rule: Physical-looking tabs (folder, binder, ledger) organize sections and act as navigation.

motion.name: Scroll-scrubbed sequence
motion.rule: Scroll position drives one product sequence on a sticky stage; reduced motion shows each step inline.

motion.name: Visitor-driven instrument
motion.rule: The visitor drags, toggles, or scrubs one control and the scene responds within 100ms with eased interpolation.

motion.name: Assembly
motion.rule: Parts of the object or document assemble into place once, as the section enters, in a 600-900ms choreographed stagger.

motion.name: Type with a pulse
motion.rule: A variable-font axis (width, weight, optical size) responds to scroll or to the scene's data; one headline, not every heading.

motion.name: Live ticker
motion.rule: Numbers in the scene count and settle as Sample events arrive; the visitor can pause and replay.

motion.name: Morph between states
motion.rule: View transitions or FLIP morph the scene between two states (before and after, raw and clustered, unpaid and paid).

worlds.name: Register or ledger
worlds.examples: ruled paper, numbered columns, posting lines, carried-forward totals, red rules
worlds.ground: ledger green or buff stock with red and blue rules

worlds.name: Printout or till roll
worlds.examples: thermal paper, dot-matrix type, perforations, itemized lines, a printed total
worlds.ground: a dark counter or desk under a white roll, so the paper is the bright thing

worlds.name: Instrument face
worlds.examples: dials, gauges, scales, needles, bezels, calibration marks
worlds.ground: enamel, anodised metal, or bakelite black behind the face

worlds.name: Dossier or binder
worlds.examples: divider tabs, rubber stamps, folders, index cards, paper clips

worlds.name: Departure or signal board
worlds.examples: split-flap rows, LED segments, status lamps, platform signage
worlds.ground: signage black, station blue, or platform enamel

worlds.name: Label, carton, or spec plate
worlds.examples: engraved plates, product labels, shipping cartons, warning stickers, rating plates

worlds.name: Chart, survey, or blueprint
worlds.examples: grid sheets, legends, soundings, contour lines, title blocks
worlds.ground: blueprint cyan or survey buff with a printed grid

worlds.name: Control panel or patch bay
worlds.examples: switches, jacks, cables, labelling tape, indicator lights

worlds.name: Newspaper or wire service
worlds.examples: mastheads, column rules, bulletins, teletype strips, datelines
worlds.ground: newsprint tint with ink-blue or black bands

worlds.name: Field notebook
worlds.examples: graph paper, pencil annotations, taped specimens, measurements in the margin
